---
title: "Tests across three or more models"
subtitle: "Example 6.2 of Mize, Doan, and Long (2019), with all four models"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

With three or more models, `mecompare` lists each model's marginal effects
and reports no differences; `metest` can be used to test the comparisons you choose. The
four nested logits of Example 6.2:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/gss_cme, clear
drop if year < 2000
drop if employed != 1
drop if missing(vhappy, college, wages, occprest, age, married, parent, woman, conserv, reltrad)

quietly logit vhappy i.college, vce(robust)
estimates store m1
quietly logit vhappy i.college i.married i.parent i.woman i.conserv i.reltrad i.year c.age##c.age, vce(robust)
estimates store m2
quietly logit vhappy i.college c.wages i.married i.parent i.woman i.conserv i.reltrad i.year c.age##c.age, vce(robust)
estimates store m3
quietly logit vhappy i.college c.wages c.occprest i.married i.parent i.woman i.conserv i.reltrad i.year c.age##c.age, vce(robust)
estimates store m4

mecompare college, models(m1 m2 m3 m4)
<</dd_do>>
```

Rows 1-4 are the effect of college in models 1-4. Whether the effect
diminishes in each subsequent model:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest, clear
metest 1 - 2, add
metest 2 - 3, add
metest 3 - 4, add
<</dd_do>>
```

And whether it is the same in all four models:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest 1 = 2 = 3 = 4
<</dd_do>>
```
